title: Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
main_claim: Let X be a compact manifold in Fujiki class C with a rational SNC boundary Delta (coefficients in [0,1], coefficient one allowed), and let f: X -> Y be a fibration. Then kappa(X, K_X+Delta) >= kappa(F, K_F+Delta_F) + kappa(f|Delta), where the last term is Campana's orbifold-base invariant. This is Campana's orbifold C_nm. Logarithmic and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity, including over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, follow as corollaries.

issues.location: sections/adjoint-addition.tex, Lemma application:weak-effectivity (Effectivity after a big base twist)
issues.description: Fujino's weak positivity theorem is applied to p'_*O(m(K_{W'/S'}+T')), where W' is only a compact Kahler/class-C manifold and S' is projective. As far as I recall, Fujino's Theorem 1.1 is stated for algebraic (complete or projective) sources. The paper does not say why it extends to a class-C source. The result is very likely true in this setting: Campana proves weak positivity in class C, and the Hodge-theoretic input (Fujino-Fujisawa) holds in the Kahler case. The paper also says it follows Campana's Remark 6.5(3) and Prop. 6.6. So this is a gap in the citation, not in the mathematics.
issues.evidence: "Fujino's weak positivity theorem applies to this log canonical pair and its projective base \cite[Theorem~1.1]{FujinoWeakPositivity}." Here W' is a Kahler modification of a class-C space, not an algebraic variety.

issues.location: sections/period-positivity.tex, proof of Theorem period:adjoint and Lemma period:rankloss
issues.description: Three deep external theorems carry the hardest step (bigness of K_S+aP): Brunebarbe-Cadorel Thm 1.1 (log general type from a generically immersive period map), Andre's monodromy normality, and Bakker-Tsimerman Ax-Schanuel. The paper invokes them without restating their exact hypotheses. Examples: quasi-finite vs. generically immersive period map; Z-VHS vs. C-VHS; strict weak Mumford-Tate subvariety on the resolved Zariski closure Z. I checked the internal logic and it holds: the rank decomposition r = d_H + s_Q, the kernel-inclusion argument, the fixed-locus bound for [N^k v], the finite-monodromy stabilizer argument, and the section-count Lemma period:subtract (asymptotics, and degree of the loss polynomial <= nu(J|E_i) < r). I did not check the hypotheses against the cited sources.
issues.evidence: "Consequently \cite[Theorem~1.1]{BrunebarbeCadorel} gives K_S+D big"; "By \cite[Theorem~1.1]{BakkerTsimermanAxSchanuel}, an intersection component of larger dimension projects into a proper algebraic weak Mumford--Tate subvariety of Z."

coverage: I read the main route line by line: the introduction and statement; Section 2 (models, log-modification discrepancy, flattening and exceptional reference, simultaneous model control, relative Iitaka construction); Section 3 (rank-one comparison); Section 4 (adjoint addition); Section 5 (period positivity); Section 6 (general-type addition via the Kovacs-Patakfalvi stable family); and the main proof plus log/ordinary corollaries in Section 7. For Section 3 this covered the root-order formula j(1+l)-1, the eigenspace lemma, descent of the tensor-power line, the extension lemma, the parabolic order beta_D, the identity T_D = min x - min(x-c) with bounds B(g,Delta) <= T <= 1, and the section comparison. For Section 5 it covered curvature and numerical dimension via full-mass potentials, the boundary restriction, the rational adjoint reduction, the stabilizer lemma, the projective period quotient, the rank-loss lemma (Ax-Schanuel H x Q decomposition, infinite and finite monodromy cases) and Lemma period:subtract. I checked these by hand: the convex combination D+M = (1-theta)E_+ + theta E_- with theta=(1-c)/(a-c) and eta=(1-c)lambda/(a-1); the twist-cancellation identity; the orbifold order inequality in the general-type addition; and the composition of inf-multiplicity bounds. I did not audit the reduced-boundary refinement (reduced-root.tex, normalization.tex) or the appendix, which the main theorem does not use. I did not check the cited external theorems against their sources.
sibling_notes: The family-033 board had two entries, both no_gap_found: Projective-Hodge-lines (rank 111) and Logarithmic-Kodaira-dimension-and-whole-fiber-variation (rank 129). The rank-129 sibling depends on this paper: its Cor 6.2 (log C_nm) and Thm 3.1 (adjoint comparison). So this audit is the upstream check for that sibling. The rank-111 sibling noted similar citation-level caveats (BBT Lemma 6.17, unstated Brunebarbe-Cadorel hypotheses), which matches my minor issue 2.
